c.tagline: Ancient marble beneath the Mediterranean sun

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing on the metro and around Monastiraki; Omónoia and Exárcheia can feel rough after dark.

hood_desc: Plaka is the picturesque old town beneath the Acropolis, a charming maze of neoclassical houses, tavernas and souvenir shops, ideal for first-time visitors wanting historic ambiance.
Monastiraki is the lively flea-market district of the old bazaar, rooftop bars with Acropolis views and buzzing streets, great for shoppers, nightlife and central sightseeing.
Kolonaki is Athens's chic, upscale neighborhood of designer boutiques, art galleries and stylish cafes on the slopes of Lycabettus, suited to luxury and fashionable travelers.
Psyrri is a gritty-turned-hip nightlife quarter packed with mezedopoleia, bars, street art and live music, perfect for younger travelers and an authentic party scene.
Koukaki is a trendy, laid-back residential area near the Acropolis Museum with local cafes and good value, appealing to travelers wanting a stylish yet relaxed base.

water.note: Tap water is treated and safe to drink, though taste varies by neighborhood.

transit.pay: You can tap a contactless bank card or phone at metro and tram gates and on buses (Tap2Ride). Otherwise buy a paper Ath.ena Ticket from station machines: a 90-minute fare is 1.20 EUR (~US$1.40), a day pass 4.10 EUR, and the 3-day tourist ticket (~20 EUR) includes one airport round trip. Airport metro trips otherwise cost about 9 EUR.
transit.hours: The metro runs about 5:30am-12:30am, with lines 2 and 3 running until ~2:30am on Friday and Saturday nights; a few bus routes run 24 hours.

transit.m: Express bus X95 to Syntagma (70 min)

landmarks: Acropolis of Athens / Parthenon
The iconic ancient citadel and its Parthenon temple crown the city, an unmistakable symbol of classical civilization.
Acropolis Museum
A sleek modern museum showcasing original Parthenon sculptures with glass floors revealing ancient ruins beneath.
Temple of Olympian Zeus
The towering Corinthian columns of this once-colossal temple make for dramatic photos framed against the Acropolis.
Panathenaic Stadium
The only stadium in the world built entirely of marble, host of the first modern Olympics in 1896.
Ancient Agora of Athens
The heart of ancient Athenian civic life, with the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus offering a glimpse of antiquity amid greenery.
Syntagma Square
Home to the Greek Parliament and the ceremonial Changing of the Evzone Guard, a colorful cultural photo opportunity.
Mount Lycabettus
Athens' highest hill offers a chapel-topped summit and the best panoramic sunset views over the entire city and Acropolis.
Plaka District
The picturesque old neighborhood beneath the Acropolis with neoclassical houses, bougainvillea-draped alleys, and tavernas.
Monastiraki Square
A bustling square and flea market with the ancient Agora, Acropolis, and a historic mosque all visible in one frame.
Roman Agora and Tower of the Winds
An ancient marketplace featuring the remarkably preserved octagonal Tower of the Winds, an early meteorological monument.

train.note: Greece currently has no international trains: Hellenic Train's cross-border services (Thessaloniki to Sofia and Skopje) are suspended until further notice, and none ever ran direct from Athens. Domestically, Hellenic Train's Athens-Thessaloniki intercity from Larissa station is the flagship route.

bus.note: International coaches use various departure points around central Athens and the Kifissos bus terminal - check your ticket. Bring your passport; border stops can add time. Domestic intercity buses are run by the regional KTEL companies.

intl.to: Ancona & Bari (Italy) - sails from Patras/Igoumenitsa, not Athens

ferry.note: No international ferries leave from Athens/Piraeus itself - Piraeus serves the Greek islands. Boats to Italy depart from Patras (~3h west of Athens by coach) and Igoumenitsa; most Italy crossings are overnight with cabins available.

half.name: Cape Sounion
half.blurb: Clifftop Temple of Poseidon crowning a headland, famed for its glorious Aegean sunsets.

half.name: Nafplio
half.blurb: Greece's first capital, an elegant seaside town below Venetian fortresses and stone lanes.

half.name: Epidaurus
half.blurb: Ancient healing sanctuary home to a magnificent theater renowned for its flawless acoustics.

half.name: Mycenae
half.blurb: Bronze Age citadel of legendary kings, entered through the imposing carved Lion Gate.

full.name: Delphi
full.blurb: Mountainside sanctuary of the ancient oracle, with the Temple of Apollo and sweeping valley views.

full.name: Meteora
full.blurb: Otherworldly monasteries perched atop soaring natural rock pillars rising above the plains.
